description: Clip-on elbow rest for a standing desk: slides onto the edge of a 19.37 mm tabletop with no screws or tools. A top plate rests on the tabletop, a 70 mm lower jaw hooks underneath to stop it lifting, and a 130 mm arm cantilevers out from the desk edge. One print per elbow; tabletop thickness, fit clearance and reach are customizer parameters.
printing_notes: Print on its side: rotate the Z-up STL 90 degrees in the slicer so a flat profile face lies on the bed. There are no overhangs, no supports are needed, and the elbow and lift loads run along the layers.
Use a brim (the footprint is about 200 x 36 mm under a 90 mm tall part), 4+ perimeters, 0.2 mm layers and 15-25% infill. PETG is preferred for sustained load.
Slide on from the front, chamfered mouth first, until the spine meets the desk edge. Check that no frame rail or cable tray sits within 70 mm of the edge; if one does, shorten under_desk.
The mouth is 19.67 mm. If it is tight, raise fit_clearance in 0.1 mm steps; if it rocks, lower it. Eased tabletop edges may need more.
Print two; the part is symmetric, so one serves either elbow.
